chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Nasr al-Baghdadi, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Ahmar, from Isma'il ibn al-Abbas ibn Yazid ibn Jubayr, from Dawud ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Rafe', from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever does not love my progeny is one of three: either a hypocrite, or born of adultery, or a person whose mother carried him in a state of impurity.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three conditions of a person who does not love the Prophet's progeny according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Imam Ali (AS) categorizes the neglect of love for the Prophet’s progeny into three distinct spiritual states: hypocrisy (nifaq), illegitimacy (zina), or impure conception (ghayr tahur). This triad underscores the Ahl al-Bayt's role as the essential criterion for verifying true faith, linking emotional devotion to theological and genealogical purity in Shia tradition.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-82 Al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abi Nasr al-Baghdady, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ja’far al-Ahmar, on the authority of Isma’il ibn al-Ab’bas ibn Yazid ibn Jobayr, on the authority of Davood ibn al-Hassan, on the authority of Abi Rafeá, on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“There are three reasons why one may not like my family. Either he is a hypocrite, was born out of adultery or was conceived when his mother was not in a purified state (that is when intercourse is not allowed).”
